text.p: CompuServe Inc said Tuesday that it and Cyber Promotions Inc will petition a federal judge to accept an agreement prohibiting the privately held Cyber Promotions from sending unsolicited e-mail to CompuServe subscribers.
The companies will petition the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio.
The order would also require Cyber Promotions to prohibit any of its customers from sending unsolicited e-mail to CompuServe subscribers, CompuServe said.

Cyber Promotions would pay $65,000 to CompuServe for legal fees incurred in obtaining the order and would also be liable for undisclosed damages to CompuServe if Cyber Promotions violated the order, CompuServe said.
CompuServe will give over $30,000 in advertising to Cyber Promotions as part of the settlement.

CompuServe said it won a temporary restraining order against Cyber Promotions in October 1996, to prevent it from configuring its unsolicited e-mail messages to appear as though they were being sent from a CompuServe computer.
The final consent order makes this permanent, CompuServe said.

"Initially CompuServe wanted a blanket block of all mail sent by Cyber Promotions to CompuServe members," said Sanford Wallace, Cyber Promotions president. "Through this settlement CompuServe agreed to not block and to allow Cyber Promotions to send mail to subscribers who wish to receive it."
